text:
maria: Quick heads-up — we need to tighten the competitive claims for the webinar + the benchmark brief. Opponents: managed cloud AI endpoints, LLM APIs, and inference infra vendors. Goal: 3 crisp battle points for SDRs + 2 bench narratives for the talk.

sam: +1. Can we prioritize latency/cost/ops tradeoffs? field teams ask for one-liners they can use in the first email.

maria: Exactly. My draft idea: "Serving-first economics: predictable p99s, lower per-token cost via batching+cache, and safer fallbacks." Thoughts?

devin: Like the direction. For the bench doc we should show two workloads: chat at 4k context and retrieval-augmented search (short prompts). Different knobs matter.

jules: For messaging, avoid heavy infra jargon in the SDR snippet. Try something like: "We reduce inference bills and outages without switching your stack." Short, provocative. :thinking_face:

tara: SDR ask: 1 sentence + quick objection response. Example: "How is this different from using cloud vendor X?" Suggested reply: "You get the same models but with predictable latency SLAs and transparent per-token economics — we tune serving not just size."

liam: I ran a quick heat test. Bench-bot uploaded a raw CSV to the drive with 1000-chat traces. Main takeaway: continuous batching reduces avg token cost by ~28% vs naive endpoint.

bench-bot: benchmark_upload: https://drive.redwood/bench/1739502468/raw_traces.csv (auto)

sam: Nice. Can we convert that into a single chart for the brief: "Cost per 1k tokens by routing strategy (hosted vs dedicated vs private)" — and then a separate latency SLO chart?

maria: Yes. Devin/Jules, can you invent two bench narratives: (A) cost-first app (batching-heavy); (B) latency-first app (p99 focus). Each one gets 2 bullets and one field script.

devin: I'll draft the cost-first narrative: 1) workload: nightly batch generation for summaries, 2) numbers: 28% lower token cost, 3) field script: "If they care about predictable monthly spend, show them reserved capacity and quantization plan."

jules: I'll handle latency-first: 1) workload: realtime chat with 200ms p95 target, 2) numbers: failover policies keep fallbacks to a cheaper variant and preserve availability, 3) field script: "Ask about p99s and how they're measured — demo a tail tracer."

tara: For SDRs, please give me 3 tested opens: 
- "How are you currently handling inference cost spikes?"
- "Would predictable latency help with your customer SLAs?"
- "We cut inference spend by X% for teams like yours — curious?"

maria: Love those. Add an objection card for "we already use X cloud" — quick counterpoints: routing/fallbacks, reserved vs burst economics, and model-variant compatibility.

liam: Also add a short comparison table row: "Operational lift" — cloud: minimal to start, grows with scale; Redwood: small upfront, predictable ops for long term. Keep it simple.

sam: One more ask — webinar hook: start with a real customer vignette (an e-comm app) that hit a 3x cost spike during peak, then show how serving-first routing and prefix cache flattened that. Story beats = pain -> solution -> numbers -> CTA.

maria: OK — next steps: Devin + Jules to drop drafts by EOD tomorrow. Sam to wire charts. Tara, I'll send the SDR opens and objection cards for quick playtest. Liam to pull the heat test chart and give a 2-sentence methodology note.

tara: I'll run a 10-min playtest with 3 SDRs on Friday morning and report back. :thumbsup:

devin: Dropping draft into the brief folder tonight: https://drive.redwood/bench/1739502468/cost_narrative.md

jules: Dropping latency draft after dinner.

maria: Thanks team. If anyone finds a hard competitor claim (e.g., "we have better model choices") — flag it here and we'll craft a neutral counter that focuses on serving-first differentiation.

sam: Noted. Also, can we author a short A/B subject line test for the webinar invite? I'll paste options in the doc.

bench-bot: reminder: meeting scheduled — Webinar narrative sync — Fri 10:00am PT (calendar invite sent).

maria: Great — wrap up for now. We'll reconvene after the playtest. :sparkles:
